newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: St Barbara says Q4 disappointing.
newsitem.headline: St Barbara says Q4 disappointing.

text.p: Gold miner St Barbara Mines Ltd said it was disappointed with a drop in production and rise in cash costs for the the fourth quarter to June 30.
Production came in at 605,423 ounces for the quarter at a cash operating cost of A$526 an ounce, compared with 635,423 ounces at a cash cost of A$403 an ounce in the preceding quarter.
Annual production was 2.60 million ounces at a cash operating cost of A$424 an ounce.

St Barbara said it ran into mining problems during each of the three months of the June quarter but said mine management had advised that the pits were generally in good order for July mining. Newly appointed executive chairman Ross Atkins said the results were obviously disppointing and directors would investigate the quarter, as well as plans for the 1997/98 year.
St Barbara also confirmed that it had written to Normandy Mining Ltd about the terms of their joint venture in the Cue District of Western Australia.

Under the original deal, announced at the start of June, St Barbara would have a 30 percent interest and Normandy a 70 stake of the venture to develop St Barbara's Cuddingwarra gold resource using Normandy's Big Bell treatment plant.
Atkins was reported on Thursday as having complained that the deal too favourable for Normandy.
St Barbara said it had written to Normandy about the proposed arrangements and was awaiting a response.
